Q: Are oauth2 and allauth similar? A:

They solve different things:

  • OAuth 2.0 is for authorization. For login, usually you use OpenID Connect (OIDC).

  • django-allauth is a Django package for signup, email verification, password reset, social/OIDC login, MFA, and account management.

  • JWT is just a token format, not a full auth strategy.

For a browser-only Django ecommerce site, better use:

Django sessions + django-allauth

It’s simpler to revoke and safer than storing JWT in browser JavaScript. For Django API with Next.js, mobile apps, or external clients, use:

Django + DRF
django-allauth for account workflows/social login
short-lived JWT access tokens
rotating refresh tokens

Avoid long-lived tokens in localStorage. Better use secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies when possible. Use OAuth/OIDC when users login with Google, Apple, Microsoft, or when another app needs access to your API. Don’t build OAuth or password handling by yourself. Next.js is not automatically “enough.” You still need auth, permissions, database transactions, payments, email, inventory, background jobs, and security. For an ecommerce system already using Django and DRF, no need to rewrite just because Next.js is trendy. A good setup is:

Django + DRF: backend, accounts, orders, payments, admin
Next.js: optional React storefront

Q: IntelliJ/AndroidStudio: icon_banner_image.xml Not Found (Snap) A:

That error isn't about your source image. ic_banner_image.xml ships inside the Android plugin itself, as the default foreground image Asset Studio uses for the TV Banner icon type. The wizard loads it from a path inside the plugin's own resources and blocks the Next button when it can't read it. So reinstalling the plugin won't help, and neither will changing your image: the file the IDE is missing is its own.

The trigger is how you installed the IDE. The Snap build from the Ubuntu Store runs under a confined, read-only filesystem, and that breaks plugins which read bundled files from disk by path, which is what Asset Studio does here.

Install IntelliJ IDEA outside Snap and it works:

- JetBrains Toolbox App: https://www.jetbrains.com/toolbox-app/

- or the .tar.gz from https://www.jetbrains.com/idea/download/ , run from the extracted folder

Reopen your project there and the wizard should generate icons fine.

If it still fails on a non-Snap install, it's an Android plugin bug, not packaging. That plugin is developed by Google, so report it on the Google Issue Tracker: https://issuetracker.google.com/

Q: Angular Application's first page very slowly to load A:

Always use latest versions of angular. Do code splitting. Lazy loading the modules reduces your initial bundle size. Remove unused imports. Try to avoid bloated third party libraries. Proper segregation of functionalities into separate modules.

Advanced: AFter doing all of the above, if you still want to reduce your bundle size. Try Using bazel for build process. https://blog.mgechev.com/2018/11/19/introduction-bazel-typescript-tutorial/

More Advanced: Still you want to reduce your bundle size. Wait for Angular Ivy(public release).
